name: Hera
tagline: ESA's first planetary defence mission, surveying Didymos and the crater left by NASA's DART
description: Hera is ESA's first planetary defence mission. It went to the binary asteroid Didymos to survey the crater and the other changes left when NASA's DART spacecraft hit its moonlet Dimorphos in 2022. OHB of Germany led the consortium of 18 ESA states that built it. It launched on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral on 2024-10-07, made a gravity assist at Mars on 2025-03-12, and weighs about 1,081 kg fully fuelled, with a body about 1.6 m on a side and solar arrays that stretch 11.5 m. It carries two Asteroid Framing Cameras, the HyperScout H imager, JAXA's thermal infrared imager TIRI, a laser altimeter and two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani. It arrived at Didymos in November 2026 and has flown a rectangular orbit around the pair since 2026-11-11. On 2026-11-25 ESA reported that the impact had flattened one face of Dimorphos into a stadium-sized crater and left it tumbling, with hundreds of boulders circling the pair, and the CubeSats are due to be deployed in January 2027.
best_known_for: The first spacecraft to stay with a binary asteroid, surveying the crater NASA's DART left
